subproblem.title: Iterated Steiner symmetrization gives a centrally symmetric compact replacement
subproblem.statement: For every d ∈ ℕ and every compact A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) there is a compact K ⊆ ℝ^d with L^d(K) = L^d(A) (L^d = volume), ediam K ≤ ediam A, and −x ∈ K for every x ∈ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → ∃ K : Set (Euclid d), IsCompact K ∧ volume K = volume A ∧ ediam K ≤ ediam A ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, -x ∈ K
proof_key_steps: Volume preservation for compact B: S_i(B) is compact by (U) and (C), hence measurable; the slice equality (L) and the coordinate Cavalieri principle (F) give L^d(S_i(B)) = L^d(B).
Finset induction over the processed coordinates, replacing K by S_i(K).
Each step preserves compactness, Lebesgue measure and the ediam bound (D), keeps the old reflection symmetries and adds R_i-symmetry (R).
After all coordinates, K is invariant under every R_i.
Flipping the coordinates of x ∈ K one at a time gives −x ∈ K.

audit.reason: The declared siblings supply every property used in the finite-coordinate induction. Compactness makes the symmetrals measurable before Cavalieri is applied. A second explicit induction converts coordinate-reflection invariance into central symmetry. All existential conclusions match the type, with no parent or self-reliance.

subproblem.title: Isodiametric inequality (Simon 2.10)
subproblem.statement: Isodiametric inequality: for every d ∈ ℕ and every set A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (not necessarily measurable or bounded), L^d(A) ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d in [0, ∞]. Here L^d = volume, ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and ediam is the extended diameter.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid d)), volume A ≤ unitBallVolume d * (ediam A / 2) ^ d
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 2.10 and its proof (book/chapter-01.txt lines 502–536) / parent steps 1a (reduction to compact sets) and 1g (conclusion).
1. ω_d ≠ 0: the open unit ball is nonempty and open, so its volume is positive (Metric.measure_ball_pos).
2. Case ediam A = ∞. Then d ≥ 1: for d = 0 every subset of the one-point space ℝ⁰ is subsingleton and has ediam 0 (ediam_subsingleton). Hence (ediam A/2)^d = (∞/2)^d = ∞ (ENNReal.top_div_of_ne_top, ENNReal.top_pow), the right-hand side is ω_d·∞ = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top, using ω_d ≠ 0), and the inequality holds.
3. Case ediam A < ∞ (reduction 1a). A is bounded (isBounded_iff_ediam_ne_top), so its closure Ā is compact (Bornology.IsBounded.isCompact_closure; ℝ^d is proper). Moreover ediam Ā = ediam A (Metric.ediam_closure) and L^d(A) ≤ L^d(Ā) (monotonicity, A ⊆ Ā).
4. By the sibling Submission.dmcbr_ci_iso_exists_symmetric_replacement applied to the compact set Ā, there is a compact K with L^d(K) = L^d(Ā), ediam K ≤ ediam Ā = ediam A, and −x ∈ K for all x ∈ K.
5. By the sibling Submission.cbr_ci_iso_volume_le_of_neg_mem, L^d(K) ≤ ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d. Since t ↦ ω_d·(t/2)^d is monotone on [0, ∞] and ediam K ≤ ediam A, ω_d·(ediam K/2)^d ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d (gcongr).
6. Hence L^d(A) ≤ L^d(Ā) = L^d(K) ≤ ω_d·(ediam A/2)^d. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unbounded A: d ≥ 1 and the right-hand side is ∞.
Bounded A: pass to the compact closure, which has the same ediam and at least the same measure.
Replace the closure by a centrally symmetric compact set of equal measure and no larger ediam (symmetric_replacement).
Apply the centrally symmetric bound (symmetric_bound) and monotonicity in ediam.

audit.reason: The infinite-diameter case and its dimension-zero exclusion are valid. Finite diameter gives compact closure without changing ediam; symmetric_replacement and symmetric_bound then give the inequality by measure and diameter monotonicity. These are exactly its declared dependencies.

subproblem.title: Lebesgue measure is at most (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d] on ℝ^d (completion of Simon 2.9)
subproblem.statement: For every d ∈ ℕ, the Lebesgue measure L^d = volume on ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is dominated by (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d]: L^d(s) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d](s) for every set s ⊆ ℝ^d (as measures, L^d ≤ (ω_d/2^d)•μH[d]). Here ω_d = unitBallVolume d = L^d(ball(0, 1)), and μH[d] is Mathlib's d-dimensional Hausdorff measure (weight diam^d, no normalising constant).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ), (volume : Measure (Euclid d)) ≤ (unitBallVolume d / 2 ^ d) • (μH[(d : ℝ)] : Measure (Euclid d))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, 'Completion of the proof of 2.9' (book/chapter-01.txt lines 547–559) / parent step 2, translated to Mathlib's normalisation of μH[d] (weight ediam^d, no normalising constant).
1. Let c := ω_d/2^d. Then c ≠ 0, since ω_d ≠ 0 (Metric.measure_ball_pos) and 2^d ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.div_ne_zero). Also c ≠ ∞, since ω_d < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top) and 2^d ≠ 0 (ENNReal.div_ne_top).
2. For every set s ⊆ ℝ^d, the sibling isodiametric inequality Submission.dmcbr_ci_iso_volume_le_ediam_pow gives L^d(s) ≤ ω_d·(ediam s/2)^d = ω_d·ediam(s)^d·(2^d)⁻¹ = c·ediam(s)^d. The ENNReal arithmetic uses a/2 = a·2⁻¹ (div_eq_mul_inv), mul_pow, ENNReal.inv_pow and commutativity. Multiplying by c⁻¹: c⁻¹·L^d(s) ≤ c⁻¹·c·ediam(s)^d = ediam(s)^d (ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel, valid as c ∉ {0, ∞}).
3. Let ν := c⁻¹•L^d, a measure. By step 2, ν(s) ≤ ediam(s)^d = ediam(s)^(d : ℝ) for every set s (ENNReal.rpow_natCast). Hence ν ≤ μH[d]. Indeed, for any δ > 0 and any countable cover (C_k) of a set B by sets with ediam C_k ≤ δ, ν(B) ≤ Σ_k ν(C_k) ≤ Σ_k ediam(C_k)^d; taking the infimum over such covers and the supremum over δ > 0 gives ν(B) ≤ μH[d](B). In Mathlib this is exactly Measure.le_hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) ν 1 one_pos: its hypothesis is required only for sets of ediam ≤ 1, and step 2 gives it for all sets.
4. For every set s: L^d(s) = c·(c⁻¹·L^d(s)) = c·ν(s) ≤ c·μH[d](s) (ENNReal.mul_inv_cancel and monotonicity of multiplication). By the setwise characterisation of ≤ for measures (Measure.le_iff'), L^d ≤ c•μH[d]. ∎
proof_key_steps: c = ω_d/2^d is positive and finite.
The isodiametric inequality rewritten: L^d(s) ≤ c·ediam(s)^d, i.e. c⁻¹L^d(s) ≤ ediam(s)^d for all s.
Multiplying back by c gives L^d ≤ c•μH[d] setwise.
